analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The patch updates the 'Last updated' date and adds a section on GPT-OSS decode command buffer partitioning (commit every 100 operations, no input-size bound). The two supplied head_text units (lines 2026-2840) are unchanged surrounding documentation. I examined them against the threat model, including T-041 and TB-007. They describe typical MTP acceptance, sampling defaults, JSON constrained answers, tool parsers, MiMo native paths and Flash-Next ownership. None of this text is part of the changed ranges, and it is not new behavior in this PR. The documentation makes no claims that weaken security controls: cache scope, the 30-minute TTL, KEK-rooted HMAC names and authenticated account scoping are not altered. It does not claim qualification beyond what the threat model states. The claims about 'approximate, not distribution-exact' typical MTP acceptance and about unqualified paths are appropriately hedged. The added GPT-OSS section is a performance tuning note. It states that results do not depend on partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. It does not touch authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or data exposure. Residual uncertainty: the underlying source change (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding) is not in the supplied batch, so I cannot verify the code. The documented claim that results are partition-independent is unverified. This is a documentation-only change here, so I report no findings.
